newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends weaker on heavy stop-loss selling.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends weaker on heavy stop-loss selling.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Monday at C$1.3869 (US$0.7210) under pressure from heavy stop-loss selling ahead of U.S. consumer prices data due out on Tuesday.
* Dealers said many domestic players were caught trying to get out of long positions as orders to sell Canadian dollars drove the unit down.

Analysts said lower-than-expected producer prices data combined with weaker retail sales data had provided little evidence of the type of inflationary pressure that could prompt the Federal Reserve to hike U.S. rates at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in early July.
That scenario frees the Bank of Canada from pressure to raise Canadian rates and avoid widening interest rate spreads.
But the U.S. government is expected to release inflation data in its report on consumer prices for May.
A Reuter survey of economists forecast consumer prices in May rose 0.2 percent.
Foreign exchange players cautioned that even if the Federal Reserve did not raise rates in July, market sentiment was resigned to eventual Fed tightening later this year.

"It's still a market pre-disposed to thinking that ultimately the Fed will be raising rates in the not-so-distant future, so that caps the upside to the Canada (dollar)," said Reid Farrill corporate foreign exchange adviser at CIBC-Wood Gundy Inc.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar dropped to 81.63 yen from Friday's 83.09 and dipped to 1.2488 marks from Friday's 1.2571 mark close.
